target_customer: Consumers with acne or hair loss who buy personalized subscription treatment kits
problem: Dermatology visits are short and lack long-term tracking, and over-the-counter acne products are one size fits all. MDacne uses a selfie to personalize a treatment kit and offers ongoing dermatologist chat support.
business_model: Consumer subscription of personalized treatment kits sold direct to consumer
product_category: AI-personalized dermatology, direct-to-consumer skin and hair care

founders.name: Oded Harth
education: AI and machine learning training at Stanford, per YC page
founders.background_notes: Forbes 30 Under 30 honoree and two-time Deloitte Fast 500 USA recipient per the YC page and company site.

founders.name: Dr. Yoram Harth
founders.background_notes: The YC launch post calls the founders a father and son team, with the father a Columbia-trained dermatologist who invented a blue light acne treatment.

competitors.name: Curology
competitors.what: Custom prescription acne treatment by subscription
competitors.traction_then: Grew mostly by word of mouth, about $20 per month, team five times larger than a year earlier

competitors.name: Proactiv
competitors.what: Mass-market acne product with large marketing presence
competitors.traction_then: Founder of Curology estimated about 3 million of 50 million US acne sufferers used it

technical_complexity.rationale: Computer vision on selfies to assess acne was a real engineering task for a small team in 2016, combined with compounding and fulfillment logistics. The models were built in-house.

defensibility.rationale: A growing image dataset helps, but rivals like Curology sold personalized treatments already and the product ingredients are common.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source opened shows an incumbent copying or buying the company. It remains independent and added MDhair in November 2021 and Nuvane later.

market_need_then: Acne is common, and the 2016 Curology coverage cited about 50 million US sufferers and strong word of mouth for personalized treatment. The MDacne app was reported in 2016 trade press and the YC launch post claimed it was the number one acne app in the App Store.

branding.domain_note: Corporate site mdalgorithms.com and product sites mdacne.com and mdhair.co.

identity.voice_and_tone: Medical authority plus democratizing dermatology with AI

branding.brand_signature: MD prefix across product brands signaling dermatologist involvement
branding.community_and_virality: The MDacne app included a community feature per the YC launch post. No merch or fan evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Product brands carry a clear medical signal, but sources show little press about the brand itself and no distinctive mascot or voice.

pivots.to: Personalized treatment kit line sold by subscription
pivots.why: Sources say the product line launched in January 2018. The reason was not stated.
Expansion using the same AI image analysis, per the November 2021 press release.

outcome_analysis: MDalgorithms launched the MDacne app in 2016, joined YC in Winter 2017 and moved into subscription treatment kits in January 2018. It added MDhair in 2021 and Nuvane later, and reported a Moxxie-backed seed round in August 2022. It stays small and independent. Funding is only partly documented and no growth figures are verified.
notes: Aggregators conflict: about $6M in June 2022 (Seedtable, StartupHub, unverified), $2.4M (Craft), $10.2M across five rounds (Bouncewatch). Only the Moxxie post confirms a seed round, dated August 12, 2022 with no amount. A March 2017 seed of $0.12M appears only on CB Insights and is unverified. User claims differ (100,000 in 2017 press release versus over 4 million in a later YC post). Company site names investors only as logos.
